title: Test FirebaseCrashlyticsService.setUserIdentifier directly instead of a hand-duplicated fake in epic_24_stop_the_bleeding_test.dart
rule: TQ-4 / PV-2 (fake diverges from the class it stands in for)
why: FirebaseCrashlyticsService.setUserIdentifier and the test's _CapturingCrashlyticsService.setUserIdentifier independently hard-code the identical `profileId == null ? '' : '$profileId'` ternary. The AC3/AC4 'no PII fallback' tests (Story 24.4, a PV-2-relevant child-privacy contract) only exercise the fake's copy. If a future change to the real class's encoding diverges from the fake -- e.g. a prefix, or an email fallback on a null check gone wrong -- this acceptance test keeps passing green while the production Crashlytics identifier regresses into leaking PII, exactly the class of bug this story exists to prevent. The sibling file (epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart) already shows the alternative -- mocktail against the real class -- is the established pattern in this codebase.
recommendation: Replace _CapturingCrashlyticsService for the identifier tests with a MockFirebaseCrashlytics (mocktail) wrapped in a real FirebaseCrashlyticsService, and verify(() => mock.setUserIdentifier('5')), matching the interaction-verification pattern already used in epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart.
acceptance_criteria: AC3/AC4 identifier tests exercise FirebaseCrashlyticsService.setUserIdentifier (via a mocked FirebaseCrashlytics), not a hand-duplicated encoding
Changing the ternary in FirebaseCrashlyticsService.setUserIdentifier without updating the test causes a test failure

corrections: A third independent duplicate of the same ternary exists at test/core/logging/crashlytics_service_test.dart:93-95, strengthening (not weakening) the finding's core claim that the real class's logic is never exercised.
